pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all 0 and CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test asserts ★ only on starred item; item() in src/index.js.

Implementation is right, but the last commit (2b8a3e5) loosened the test's status assertion from toBe(200) to toBeDefined(), which can never fail; the 200 status of the starred view is no longer checked. Order/content still asserted, so partially evidenced.
'AC-4' test checks / and /?show=all give id-ordered full list.
'AC-5' test checks exact link markup on both views.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty, __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards.

findings.what: Commit 2b8a3e5 'Follow-up edits' weakened `expect(res.status).toBe(200)` to `expect(res.status).toBeDefined()`, an assertion that can never fail. A starred view returning 500 or 400 with the right body would not be caught by this status check.
The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened the AC-3 status assertion. The commit message 'Follow-up edits' also hides this.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or disclose the change; give the commit a descriptive message.

findings.what: npm test could not be run here (vitest not installed), so the suite was not executed by this review.

lenses.note: Spec present; implementation matches decisions (order kept, query param). No extra behaviour beyond the traffic-checker query allowance, which is disclosed and needed for AC-7.
All four state rows have tests; AC-3 test weakened in the last commit.
A late commit replaced toBe(200) with toBeDefined().
Whitelist via Object.hasOwn, parameterless SQL built from constants; correct.
Titles are HTML-escaped; show is whitelisted; no injection path found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond server-rendered HTML strings in src/index.js; no stylesheets or components.
No browser flow or screenshots in the change; HTML is checked by the tests.
